metas.name: Botswana - A33 Lush Landscape
metas.note:
• The A33 is characterised by a landscape that is more lush than usual.
  • Trees have lots of green leaves and the grass is very tall.
  • The more north you go, the more lush the vegetation becomes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - A35 Power Line
metas.note:
The A35 is a very recognisable road:

  • There is always a power line to your west.
  • It can also be recognised by its grainy asphalt with faded markings.
  • Many small tracks can be found parallel to the road, disappearing into the bushes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Francistown Antennas
metas.note:
• In Francistown, you can often see a lone hill with radio antennas, which is located on the north side of the city.
  • This hill is a good way to distinguish Francistown from Gaborone.

NOTE:

  • The town of Serowe has a similar hill with antennas.
  • Here, the towers are taller, red-and-white striped, and the hill has a flat top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Gaborone
metas.note:
• Gaborone is the capital and largest city.
  • It tends to look richer and more developed than the rest of Botswana, though some neighbourhoods may still look impoverished.
  • In some southern parts of the city hills can be seen, but most of the town is flat.

NOTE:

  • The only other place in the country that often looks similar is Francistown.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Hills
metas.note:
• Most of Botswana is as flat as a pancake.
  • If you see hills, you are most likely in one of the two areas indicated on the minimap.

NOTE:

  • Even in the indicated areas, there are a lot of very flat areas, as many of Botswana’s hills are geographically isolated.
  • Some lone hills may also appear far outside the indicated areas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Maun Bright Sand
metas.note: • Maun is the only relatively large city in Botswana that has this bright white sandy soil, which is typical for the middle western region of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Red Road
metas.note:
• The road that runs along Botswana’s southern border, through the town of Middlepits, has asphalt with a distinct red tint.
  • The landscape is arid.
  • In some sections, slight hills can be seen.

NOTE:

  • Near the town of Middlepits itself, the soil is very red and dotted with small white pebbles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Red Soil
metas.note:
• The landscape in the eastern pocket north of Francistown is characterised by red soil and a somewhat arid look.
  • The soil in these two areas often looks firm and rocky, rather than sandy or dusty.
  • Trees and bushes with yellowed leaves and other “autumn” colours are common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Semi Arid Hills
metas.note:
• The southeastern region near Gaborone has many semi-arid hills covered in short shrubs.
  • If you see a lot of these, you are likely to be in the area between Gaborone and Lobatse.

NOTE:

  • Similar hills can be found elsewhere in the country and across the border in South Africa.
  • If you see a large quantity of them, and use other clues to rule out South Africa, you can be fairly certain that you are in southeastern Botswana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - White Sandy Soil
metas.note:
• A large region in the middle western part of the country is characterised by very white sandy soil.
  • In addition, the vegetation tends to look very dry.

NOTE:

  • Sandy soil can be found in many places in Botswana.
  • This tip specifically refers to the bright white colour of the sand.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Dark Greenness
metas.note:
• This distinct region in the central South of the country, mostly along the MR9, can be recognized by the dark, overwhelming greenness and tall wooded mountains.

NOTE:

  • If you are struggling to see why this is unique, try comparing this to other areas of the country, which are more “golden” and light-coloured.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Flat Landscape
metas.note: • You can recognise this region in the east of the country thanks to the unusual flatness and the mountains often visible in the distance.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Pine Trees
metas.note:
• Pine tree plantations are found in select areas in the West of the country.

NOTE:

  • Similar plantations can also be found in South Africa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Pristine Golden Grass
metas.note:
• Montane grasslands with long golden grass and a mountainous landscape are typical of Western Eswatini.

NOTE:

  • Long grass can be found in almost all areas of Eswatini.
  • This clue refers specifically to the pristine golden colour most commonly seen in the Western highlands.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Sugar Cane
metas.note: • Sugar cane is grown in several areas along the Eastern border.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Dense Forests
metas.note:
• Dense forests in Ghana are typically found in the southwest and east.
  • You will usually see many naturally occurring palm trees, making the two regions recognizable.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Palm Trees
metas.note:
• Tall palm trees are commonly found along the coast.
  • Most of them are located in the west.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Peeled Tape
metas.note: • In the east and north, you can find the ‘peeled tape’, which unlike the ‘unpeeled tape’, is slightly peeled off.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Savannah Landscape
metas.note: • Northern Ghana features a savannah landscape, which can be identified by its dry soil and less dense vegetation.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Scotched Tape
metas.note: • North of Kumasi, and west of Tamale, you can find this ‘scotched tape’, which has two distinct white spots on the left side of the tape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Tall Mountains
metas.note:
• Tall mountain ranges in Ghana are typically seen near Lake Volta in the highlighted area.

NOTE:

  • Mountain ranges to the east are more common in the area near Togo.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Unpeeled Tape
metas.note: • In the southwest, you can find the ‘unpeeled tape’, which is essentially a mostly intact tape, which is not peeling off.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - A1 Northwest
metas.note:
• The northwest part of the country has very limited coverage, most of which is on the A1 or in Sibiloi National Park.
  • It has faintly tan soil and sparse low trees.
  • A lot of the coverage in this area is very flat, but you can also see hills or mountains.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - A109 Cord & Orange Dirt
metas.note:
• The A109 between Mombasa and Nairobi has light orange dirt and many hills around the road and in the distance.
  • Most of the coverage between Mombasa and Emali also has a unique car, which has a cord on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Agriculture Parts
metas.note:
• The far west areas of the country that are northwest and southwest of Kisumu are the most agricultural parts of the country.
  • You will often see farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus trees in this region of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Dirt Car
metas.note: • This car that is covered in specks of dirt is unique to these stretches of the A3, B9, and the Habaswein-Dadaab Road connecting the two.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Mombasa White Sand
metas.note: • Mombasa and the other coastal towns are easily identified from the white sandy soil, palm trees and coastal feel.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Semi-Arid Kitui
metas.note: • The area around Kitui is semi-arid, usually mountainous, and has light orange, sandy dirt.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - White Tape
metas.note: • You can see pieces of white tape on the roof of the Google car in a lot of the coverage north and south of Nairobi.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - A2 Road Quality
metas.note: • The section of the A2 between Maseru and Mafeteng has by far the best road quality in all of Lesotho.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - A25 Katse Reservoir
metas.note:
• There are two large man-made water reservoirs in the mountainous part of Lesotho, which can be seen from several road sections.
  • The larger Katse reservoir is visible from parts of the A25.

NOTE:

  • Do not confuse these with the small industrial lake found near the Letseng diamond mine.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - A25 Raindrops
metas.note: • On a section of the A25, just east of the big reservoir, the camera is covered in raindrops in one direction.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - A3 Off-Road Mohale Reservoir
metas.note:
• There are two large man-made water reservoirs in the mountainous part of Lesotho, which can be seen from several road sections.
  • The smaller Mohale reservoir is visible from an off-road of the A3.

NOTE:

  • Do not confuse these with the small industrial lake found near the Letseng diamond mine.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - A5 Tempoary Bollard
metas.note:
• Several sections of the A5 south of Nyakosoba are under construction.
  • As a result, you will often see a sort of temporary “bollard” next to the road, consisting of a stick that is mostly painted white.
  • Even on sections without the bollard, you can often recognize this road, as it is a wide dirt road with very dark brown soil.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Flat Region
metas.note:
Lesotho Flat Region:

  • In the flat region, the road itself runs through a mostly flat or hilly landscape.
  • “Flat” is a bit of a misnomer, as you will usually still see tabletop-like mountains around you.
  • However they will usually be significantly further away from the road, giving you a more clear line of sight.
  • This “flat” part is the region with the most coverage, settlements and agriculture.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Maseru
metas.note:
• The only city with a significantly urbanised downtown area is Maseru, the capital.
  • All other towns have a very provincial feel in comparison to Maseru.

NOTE:

  • The suburbs of Maseru can still have a very rural feel.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Mountainous Region
metas.note:
Lesotho Mountainous Region:

  • In the mountainous part, the road will usually be directly on the side of the mountain, instead of slightly away from it.
  • The mountains are often large, closer to the road, and covered in green grass.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Qacha's Nek
metas.note:
• Qacha's Nek is a very recognizable town that is located far away from most other towns, on the southeastern border with South Africa.
  • It is situated right in the middle of green mountains, and it had noticeably bad weather when the Google car drove there.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Ramatsediso Road
metas.note:
The road going from Ramatsediso to Sehlabathebe NP, in the southeast on the border with South Africa, is very recognizable.

➖➖➖➖➖

Consider guessing there if the following three things are all true for your location:

  • Unpaved road with light brown soil.
  • Good weather with little fluffy clouds.
  • Grassy landscape high in the mountains.

You will also often be able to see exposed, light-coloured rocks next to the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Abuja Exposed Rock
metas.note: • These monolithic mountains with exposed, weathered rock are common in and around Abuja.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Benue State
metas.note:
• Benue state can be recognized by the lush, green grass covered ground, with reddish soil.
  • The vegetation is somewhat scattered, with the grass making way for taller trees.
  • Thatched huts are also common in comparison to other southern states.

NOTE:

  • An abundance of palms should make you lean toward the bordering southern states that can look similar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Christian: South
metas.note:
• Nigeria is mainly Christian in the south, and Islamic in the north.
  • As such, seeing women in hijabs and men in muslim attire is more common in the north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Islamic: North
metas.note:
• Nigeria is mainly Christian in the south, and Islamic in the north.
  • As such, seeing women in hijabs and men in muslim attire is more common in the north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Kaduna State
metas.note: • These haystacks are extremely common and are almost exclusively found in Kaduna state.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Kano State
metas.note:
• If you find yourself in an arid, but green, agricultural landscape with an abundance of corn around, you are likely to be in Kano state.
  • It is only covered by shitcam, without any Generation 3 or 4.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Niger State
metas.note:
• Niger state is the shitcam equivalent to Benue state.
  • It is almost entirely covered by shitcam, and can be recognized by the scattered trees, reddish soil, and dry grass.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Open Landscape
metas.note:
• The highways that run through the northwestern states of Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, and Katsina can be recognized by an even more open and arid landscape compared to Niger state.
  • The tree coverage becomes even more sparse, or there may not be trees at all.
  • These states are entirely covered by shitcam.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Rocky Landscape
metas.note:
• A savannah landscape combined with rocky hills can most commonly be seen in the northeast in the states of Plateau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, and the north of Taraba.
  • The hills in the far east and west of this region are typically greener and covered in more vegetation compared to the hills toward the middle of the range.

NOTE:

  • Around the city of Gombe, hills composed of softer, clay-like soil can be seen instead.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Akagera National Park
metas.note:
• The Akagera national park features a very vegetated yet dry landscape with wide unpaved roads that are reddish-brown in colour.
  • You can also find rectangular waystones at intersections.
  • This coverage was taken with the brown Google car.

NOTE:

  • There is some coverage on the paved section south of the national park.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Black Truck
metas.note:
• The black pickup truck can be found in most of Kigali.

NOTE:

  • The white car will be found everywhere in the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Brown Truck
metas.note:
• The brown pickup truck can be found in many small pockets around Rwanda.

NOTE:

  • The white car will be found everywhere in the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Lower Elevation
metas.note:
• Northeastern Rwanda has less extreme elevation compared to the rest of Rwanda.
  • It more so consists of rolling hills and open agricultural land or undeveloped grassland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Tea Plantations
metas.note: • Tea plantations are common in Western Rwanda, and a couple other pockets.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Volcanoes
metas.note: • Volcanoes and volcanic rocks can be seen in northwestern Rwanda.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Diourbel Region
metas.note:
• Diourbel Region is the only region in Senegal with extensive rural coverage.
  • The coverage in the region will look like this, with the Google Car driving on a sandy road with sparse trees.
  • Some of the coverage extends to the west in the Thies region up to Babou.

NOTE:

  • The sand in the coverage around Touba tends to be more grassy.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Dry Hills
metas.note: • A dry landscape with slight hills can mostly be seen around Bakel, but also south to Nayé.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Green Hills
metas.note: • A greener landscape with larger hills can be seen around Kedougou and Mako.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Irrigated Rice Fields
metas.note: • Irrigated rice fields can sometimes be seen in the region between St Louis and Richard Toll.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Landscape North
metas.note:
• The landscape north of The Gambia and for Senegal generally is a flat, arid, savannah-desert landscape with sparse trees.
  • The trees themselves will be somewhat short and have leaves that are faded in colour.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Landscape South
metas.note:
• The vegetation in the region south of The Gambia is more lush and green compared to the rest of Senegal, and palm trees can be seen closer to the coast.

NOTE:

  • Coverage toward the west will also be especially tropical.
  • In addition, make sure not to confuse the south with some coverage near Dakar, which can look deceivingly green.
  • However, here the vegetation will look a lot more low and coastal.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Rolling Landscape
metas.note: • A very slightly rolling landscape consisting of vegetated sand dunes can be seen along the northwestern coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Silver Car Antenna
metas.note:
• The silver Generation 4 car with a long antenna at the front left can be seen on many roads, but none past the eastern border of Diourbel Region.

NOTE:

  • The antenna is visible even if the car is blurred.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - White Car
metas.note: • The regular Generation 4 white car is most commonly found south of The Gambia, but can also be found on the northeastern coast and a small region between Kaolack and Saly.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Alternating Insulators Pole
metas.note:
• Poles with 3 alternating insulators sticking out horizontally at the top are mostly seen in the four northern provinces of Limpopo, Gauteng, North West and Mpumalanga.
  • They can also sometimes be found in Northern Cape.
  • In the rest of the country, these pole tops are exceedingly rare.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Bird Nest Pole
metas.note: • Big bird nests on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Cook Pine Trees
metas.note:
• Uniquely tall Cook pine trees are found mostly between the cities of East London and Durban along the southeastern coast.

NOTE:

  • These are planted and not native, so they can be found anywhere along the coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Dry Landscape & Red Soil
metas.note: • A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Eastern Cape Pole
metas.note: • A similar poletop can be found in Eastern Cape, however the A-shape is noticeably wider and the bottom insulators are attached directly to the ‘A’ rather than a horizontal bar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Flat & Subtropical Vegetation
metas.note: • The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably flat, with green subtropical vegetation.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Grainy Pavement
metas.note: • You can find this grainy, almost Texas-like pavement with a hint of pink in Limpopo.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Grassy Rolling Hills
metas.note:
• Grassy rolling hills are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town.
  • Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Kruger Park Car
metas.note:
• A camouflage car with black side mirrors and roof racks can be seen in Kruger National Park, on the Mozambique border.

NOTE:

  • The Park now also has generation 4 coverage, without the car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - KwaZulu-Natal Pole
metas.note: • Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Limpopo Pole
metas.note: • Poles with 2 diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape can be found mostly in the northeastern provinces, most commonly in Limpopo and North West.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Mpumalanga Pole
metas.note:
• Poles with 1 or 2 metal arms holding up insulators are most commonly seen in Mpumalanga.

NOTE FROM MYSELF:

  • These poles are very rare in my opinion.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Northeast Landscape
metas.note:
• The northeast of the country can look very dry and somewhat barren, with a lot of orange or red soil.
  • You will often see hills or mountains covered in shrubs.

NOTE:

  • Depending on the season, the coverage can change drastically from dry to very green.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Pine Tree Plantations
metas.note:
• Tree plantations that consist mostly of pine are common to the west of Eswatini, and some to the south in KwaZulu-Natal.

NOTE:

  • Pine tree plantations are typically seen within the country of Eswatini itself.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Power Plants
metas.note: • Power plants are often seen in between the town of Secunda and eMalahleni in Mpumalanga.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Red Sticker
metas.note:
• Square, red stickers on the back of regular signs are often found in Eastern cape and close to Eastern cape in Northern Cape and Free State.
  • You may see them in the North West province as well, but to a lesser extent.

NOTE:

  • Red stickers on the back of chevrons can be seen in almost every province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Rocky Mountains
metas.note:
• Unique rocky, treeless mountains can be seen in Western Cape, with most of the mountains having tall, steep sides and sharp peaks.

NOTE:

  • Similar mountains can be seen in and around Lesotho.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Sugarcane Plantations
metas.note:
• Sugarcane plantations are most commonly seen in KwaZulu-Natal, mostly along the coast.
  • However, they can also be seen in Mpumalanga on the Mozambique border.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Vineyards
metas.note:
• Vineyards are almost exclusively found in Western Cape, mostly in valleys near the coast.
  • You can also commonly find them near Upington, in Northern Cape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Western Cape Pole
metas.note: • Poles with 3 bars forming the letter ‘A’, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - White Sticker
metas.note: • White stickers on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Dark Green Mazda
metas.note:
• The dark green Mazda is the most common follow car in Tunisia.
  • This becomes apparent if you look at the coverage map, it can be found all the way from Hammamet to Djerba.
  • Aside from the darker colour, it can also be recognized by its military licence plate with a red strip on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Desert Landscape
metas.note:
• South of Gabes is where the landscape changes into something more akin to a desert.
  • A lot more rubbish and small white rocks can be found along the roads.
  • Olive tree plantations are still somewhat common.
  • A mountain range far in the distance is often visible to the southwest.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Djerba Follow Car
metas.note:
• The island of Djerba is the only region of Tunisia where you are usually not accompanied by a follow car.
  • Most coverage completely lacks one.
  • While it is rare, this white Mercedes and the dark green follow car can be present.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Djerba Vibe
metas.note:
• The island of Djerba can sometimes have a distinct vibe.
  • There tend to be a lot of palm trees. Whitewashed, traditional buildings with blue doors and windows are common.

NOTE:

  • Not all locations on the island will have this distinct vibe.
  • A lack of a follow car is another good way to confirm that you are on Djerba
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Flat & Arid Landscape
metas.note:
• The large middle region between Hammamet and Gabes is very flat, and more arid.
  • Olive tree plantations are common and the more south you go, the drier the landscape becomes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Hilly Terrain
metas.note:
• The area north of Tunis has a Mediterranean climate with hilly terrain.
  • The region is very agricultural and at the time the coverage was captured, almost all fields laid fallow.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Kairouan Follow Car
metas.note:
• The city of Kairouan in central-northern Tunisia has this unique follow car, a white Mitsubishi.
  • The dark green follow car can also sometimes be spotted following the Mitsubishi.

NOTE:

  • Some white follow cars in Tunisia can look similar to the Kairouan car. However, none of them are Mitshubishis.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Light Green Toyota
metas.note:
• This light green Toyota follow car can be found everywhere in the northernmost part of Tunisia.
  • You will never see it south of Hammamet.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Tunis Follow Cars
metas.note:
• Tunis, the capital of Tunisia, has a lot of different follow cars.
  • Most of them can be found all over the city.
  • The light green Toyota can also be spotted here.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Vegetated Hills
metas.note: • The area between Tunis and Hammamet looks similar to the area north of Tunis, but the hills tend to be higher and more vegetated.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.
